newsitem.title: USA: Senators urge Reno to sue tobacco firms.
newsitem.headline: Senators urge Reno to sue tobacco firms.

text.p: Five Democratic senators on Tuesday asked Attorney General Janet Reno to file suit against major tobacco companies to recoup the U.S. federal government's cost of treating smoking-related illnesses.
In a letter to Reno the senators estimated the government spent about $20 billion a year through Medicare, Medicaid and other federal health programmes on tobacco-related expenses.
They urged her to join the host of state attorneys general who have sued tobacco firms to recover their own costs of treating such illnesses.

"We are writing to strongly urge that you follow the lead of 23 state attorneys general in seeking to recover the approximately $20 billion in tobacco-related health care costs borne by federal taxpayers each year," the letter said.
"We know you have been considering options for legal action in this area. We urge you to act promptly to have the federal government join the states in taking action," it said.
The Justice Department had no immediate comment.

The letter comes in the midst of highly publicised negotiations between state attorneys general and tobacco companies. The tobacco firms hope to negotiate a settlement to state lawsuits asking them to pay the Medicaid costs of treating smoking-related illness.
At the White House, deputy White House counsel Bruce Lindsey received an update on the progress of the settlement talks from Mississippi Attorney General Michael Moore, a key negotiator in the talks.
The parties in the talks are probably going to meet again later this week, a White House official said.

The two sides are talking about a plan under which industry would provide up to $300 billion in compensation over 25 years and accept a host of new federal regulations. In return, the industry wants broad immunity from future lawsuits filed by smokers.

The senators said the federal government should also seek compensation for its share of such costs. They estimated Medicare spent $10 billion a year on smoking-related illness; Medicaid $5 billion and other health programmes another $5 billion.
"The government shouldn't waste this opporuntity to bill the tobacco industry for robbing the health and well-being of the American people," said Iowa Democratic Sen. Tom Harkin.
Democratic senators signing the letter were Harkin, Frank Lautenberg of New Jersey, Dick Durbin of Illinois, Paul Wellstone of Minnesota and Ron Wyden of Oregon.

At a news conference, several of the senators said they had not talked to Reno directly about the issue. But they said they had been led to believe by Clinton administration staff aides that they would be supportive of the proposal.
